208: 
209: \paragraph{Replay and numerical checks.}
210: The post-outcome audit replays the original representation optimizer with
211: fixed logged actions and rewards for all 600 trajectories; it never replaces
212: a behavior action or generates a new observation.  It reconstructs
213: collection-time category weights and compares the resulting sandwich,
214: effective widths, and recommendations at the stored states.  Matrix, center,
215: and endpoint reconstruction are checked at rounds 1, 2, 10, 100, 500, and 1000;
216: the original float64 tolerances are retained.  These computations check an
217: implementation of the mathematical construction, without converting
218: floating-point residuals into verified certificates.  All declared checks
219: passed; the largest residual divided by its original tolerance was below
220: $0.005$.  The per-seed variation in the preceding table was reproduced by this
221: separate fixed-action replay.
222: 
223: \paragraph{How to read the width and regret comparisons.}
224: The upper panel of \Cref{tab:transport-followup-relative-audit} compares each
225: effective width with its reference width before averaging.  The lower panel
226: asks what immediate expected reward is lost by the recommendations on those
227: same states.  It does not accumulate the outcomes of a policy that follows
228: those recommendations over time.

248: \paragraph{What the timing records leave out.}
249: Fixed-state kernel timings are retained in the audit artifact.  They were
250: collected under parallel analysis load and exclude matrix construction,
251: confidence estimation, and the policy loop, so they do not establish
252: end-to-end speedup.  The category construction requires additional
253: accumulated collection weights and still uses matrix solves and the frozen
254: confidence construction.
